subtitle: B2 · Unit 8: B2 · Education, culture and identity: synthesize what people say

steps.title: Reported speech: preserve the speaker, time and degree of certainty
steps.body: When you report an idea, make clear whose idea it is. With a present reporting verb, the original time often stays the same (elle dit qu'elle participe). With a past reporting verb, French often shifts the time reference: present → imperfect, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, future → conditional. Keep the shift only when the reporting time calls for it; do not change a statement just to make it sound formal. Direct quotation preserves exact wording; paraphrase preserves the meaning in your own words.

steps.title: Reported speech: preserve the speaker, time and degree of certainty
rows: Elle dit qu'elle apprend en échangeant.
She says she learns by exchanging ideas.
Elle a dit qu'elle apprenait en échangeant.
She said she learned by exchanging ideas.
Il a expliqué qu'il avait suivi un atelier.
He explained that he had attended a workshop.
She announced that she would return.
Il explique avoir changé de démarche.
He explains having changed his approach.

steps.prompt: A present-tense report: Elle dit qu'elle ___ en groupe.
steps.explain: With elle dit, the reported present can remain present.

steps.prompt: Past report of a completed earlier action: Il a expliqué qu'il ___ un atelier.
steps.explain: The plus-que-parfait marks a completed action earlier than the past report.
